items.title: Deep Learning
items.authors: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville
items.summary: The standard deep learning textbook, from linear algebra basics to generative models. Free to read online.

items.title: Dive into Deep Learning
items.authors: Aston Zhang, Zachary C. Lipton, Mu Li, Alexander J. Smola
items.summary: Every chapter is runnable code. Learn deep learning by building it, with PyTorch, JAX and more.

items.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
items.authors: Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jonathan Taylor
items.summary: The friendliest serious intro to ML: regression, trees, resampling and more, with R and Python labs. Free PDF.

items.title: The Elements of Statistical Learning
items.authors: Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jerome Friedman
items.summary: The deeper, math-heavy companion to ISL. A reference you'll return to for years. Free PDF.

items.title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
items.summary: A classic treatment of ML through the lens of probability. Now free as a PDF from Microsoft Research.

items.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
items.authors: Marc Peter Deisenroth, A. Aldo Faisal, Cheng Soon Ong
items.summary: Linear algebra, calculus and probability, taught exactly as ML uses them. Free PDF.

items.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
items.summary: Build a digit-recognizing network from scratch and really understand backprop. Clear, free and online.

items.title: Understanding Deep Learning
items.summary: A modern, beautifully illustrated textbook covering transformers, diffusion and more. Free PDF.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
items.authors: Richard S. Sutton, Andrew G. Barto
items.summary: The foundational RL textbook: bandits, MDPs, TD learning, policy gradients. Free PDF.

items.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
items.summary: A broad, up-to-date survey of ML from a probabilistic view. Free draft PDF.

items.title: Think Stats
items.summary: Learn statistics by doing it in Python with real data sets. Free online as notebooks.

items.title: Interpretable Machine Learning
items.summary: How to explain what a model learned: feature importance, SHAP, partial dependence and more. Free online.

items.title: Speech and Language Processing
items.summary: The NLP textbook, from n-grams to large language models. Free draft chapters.

items.title: The Illustrated Transformer
items.summary: The picture-by-picture walkthrough of attention that made transformers click for a generation of engineers.

items.title: Understanding LSTM Networks
items.summary: A crisp, diagram-led explanation of how LSTMs remember and forget.

items.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Recurrent Neural Networks
items.summary: Character-level RNNs writing Shakespeare and code. A fun, inspiring read.

items.title: A Recipe for Training Neural Networks
items.summary: Hard-won, practical steps for getting a network to actually train. Read before your first real project.

items.title: Yes You Should Understand Backprop
items.summary: Why leaky abstractions mean you need to know what gradients do under the hood.

items.title: Calculus on Computational Graphs: Backpropagation
items.summary: Backprop explained as the chain rule on a graph. Short and clarifying.

items.title: The Bitter Lesson
items.summary: A two-page essay on why general methods that scale with compute keep winning. Widely cited.

items.title: Why Momentum Really Works
items.summary: Interactive figures show exactly how momentum speeds up gradient descent.

items.title: A Gentle Introduction to Graph Neural Networks
items.authors: Benjamin Sanchez-Lengeling, Emily Reif, Adam Pearce, Alexander B. Wiltschko
items.summary: An interactive tour of learning on graphs: molecules, social networks and more.

items.title: Feature Visualization
items.authors: Chris Olah, Alexander Mordvintsev, Ludwig Schubert
items.summary: See what individual neurons in a vision network respond to.

items.title: What are Diffusion Models?
items.summary: A thorough, math-forward explainer of the models behind modern image generation.

items.title: Rules of Machine Learning
items.summary: 43 practical rules for shipping ML in production, from Google.

items.title: A Few Useful Things to Know About Machine Learning
items.summary: Folk wisdom on overfitting, features and generalization that textbooks rarely spell out.

items.title: Attention Is All You Need
items.summary: The paper that introduced the transformer, the architecture behind today's language models.

items.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
items.authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun
items.summary: Skip connections made very deep networks trainable. One of the most cited papers in ML.

items.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
items.authors: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Geoffrey E. Hinton
items.summary: AlexNet: the 2012 result that kicked off the deep learning boom.

items.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
items.summary: The default optimizer for most deep learning. Short and readable.

items.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
items.authors: Nitish Srivastava, Geoffrey Hinton, Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Ruslan Salakhutdinov
items.summary: Randomly switching off neurons during training: a simple idea with a big effect.

items.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
items.authors: Tomas Mikolov, Kai Chen, Greg Corrado, Jeffrey Dean
items.summary: Word2vec: words as vectors, where king − man + woman ≈ queen.

items.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
items.authors: Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova
items.summary: Pre-train once, fine-tune everywhere. BERT reset the bar on language tasks.

items.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
items.summary: GPT-3 showed that a big enough language model can learn new tasks from a few examples in the prompt.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
items.summary: Loss falls predictably as you scale model size, data and compute.

items.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
items.authors: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, Pieter Abbeel
items.summary: The paper that made diffusion models a practical way to generate images.

items.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
items.summary: Why the model is the smallest part of a real ML system, and where the hidden costs live.

items.title: Neural Networks
items.summary: The best visual intuition for neural networks, gradient descent and backprop, in animated lessons.

items.title: Seeing Theory
items.summary: Interactive, visual introduction to probability and statistics from Brown University.

items.title: Machine Learning Crash Course
items.summary: Google's free, fast-paced intro with videos, visualizations and exercises.
